submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 at 4 cm thickness is recommended based on the following analysis:

PERFORMANCE: R3 at 4 cm achieves 3.732σ pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c, which is the best performance among radiators that meet the humidity ageing constraint. This represents a 31% improvement over R2 (the only other compliant option at 2.838σ).

HUMIDITY AGEING COMPLIANCE: R3 features a hydrophobic treatment specifically designed to protect the porous radiator material from humidity damage. This treatment is critical for meeting the hard requirement that transparency loss not exceed 10% after the 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test. The hydrophobic coating prevents moisture absorption that would otherwise degrade the optical properties of the porous material.

EXCLUSION OF R1: Although R1 shows the highest raw separation performance (up to 4.493σ at 3 cm), it is a porous radiator without any protective treatment. Porous materials are inherently vulnerable to humidity-induced degradation, and without hydrophobic protection, R1 would likely fail the 10-year humidity ageing test requirement. Since the radiator cannot be replaced during the run, R1 must be excluded.

EXCLUSION OF R2: While R2 as a solid radiator likely meets the humidity constraint, its lower refractive index results in significantly worse separation performance (2.838σ at best) compared to R3.

THICKNESS OPTIMIZATION: Systematic simulation across 1-6 cm range shows R3 peaks at 4 cm thickness (3.732σ), with performance degrading at both lower (3.558σ at 3 cm) and higher (3.326σ at 5 cm) thicknesses.

requirements.evidence: R3 features a hydrophobic treatment specifically designed to protect against humidity damage. This treatment prevents moisture absorption in the porous material, ensuring the radiator will meet the 10-year ageing requirement. R1 (porous without protection) would likely fail this test and is therefore excluded despite higher raw performance.
The recommended thickness of 4 cm falls within the specified range of 1-6 cm.
